newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.S. peacekeepers confiscate Bosnian army weapons.
newsitem.headline: U.S. peacekeepers confiscate Bosnian army weapons.

text.p: U.S. troops confiscated hundreds of Kalashnikov assault rifles and tonnes of ammunition from a Bosnian army headquarters on Thursday in enforcement of the Dayton peace agreement, NATO said.

The American peacekeepers also towed away two Bosnian armoured personnel carriers although Moslem civilians in the village of Celic tried to block the removal by forming a human barrier in the street.
"We let the American tanks pass but we stood in front of the American trucks," a 28-year-old woman named Dalko told Reuters.
"Then the Americans got out of the vehicles and wrestled with us... We thought the Americans might shoot us so we had to let them go."

NATO, which leads the Dayton peace implementation force, charged that the Bosnian Army's 254 Brigade had instigated a violent incident in Gajevi, near Celic, on Tuesday, in which several people were killed and a number of others wounded by gunfire.

NATO forces and U.N. police also raided a Serb police station in Koraj, east of Gajevi, on Wednesday and confiscated weapons found there. NATO said the Serb police had used the weapons to fire at Moslems in Gajevi on Tuesday.

NATO vowed to destroy all of the confiscated arms and ammunition and to ban all weapons in a 35 square km (13 square miles) "Temporary Restriction Zone" around Celic. The alliance will begin enforcing the zone on Saturday.

NATO spokesman Major Brett Boudreau said the U.S. troops arrived unannounced at the 254 Brigade headquarters outside Celic at 5 a.m. on Thursday and removed several hundred Kalashnikovs and two five-tonne trucks of ammunition.
He said civilians had blocked the passage of the Americans in an action which he described as "short-lived but serious and potentially threatening".
"Some rocks and stones were thrown at us and some of our personnel had to physically lift protesters off the road. Once they saw we were determined they made way," the NATO spokesman said.
